Bulk fermentation is the long rise after the dough is mixed with the levain and before shaping. The dough should grow by about half and become airy, jiggly and domed at the edges. Warm dough ferments faster, so a kitchen at 24 degrees might need four hours where a cold one needs eight. Stretch and folds every half hour in the first two hours build gluten strength. Underproofed loaves are dense with a tight crumb; overproofed dough spreads flat. The starter's health decides most of this, see [[Sourdough starter]].
